title: ICC Moves Into WADA's Top Compliance Tier Ahead of Cricket's Olympic Return
excerpt: WADA upgraded the ICC from tier 2 to tier 1 from January 1 because of cricket's Olympic inclusion, putting cricket under the strictest compliance monitoring — timely testing, whereabouts pursuit and three-month deadlines to fix critical failures.
body:
• The World Anti-Doping Agency has upgraded the International Cricket Council from tier 2 to tier 1 under its prioritisation policy, with the new tiers taking effect from January 1.
  • WADA said federation tiers are based on whether a sport is in the Olympic or Paralympic programme and on Minimum Levels of Analysis — cricket returns to the Olympics at Los Angeles 2028 after more than 100 years.
  • Tier 1 brings the strictest scrutiny: timely sample collection, pursuit of all whereabouts failures and potential violations, and fair hearings by an impartial, operationally independent panel.
  • India remained in the top tier of signatories facing the strictest scrutiny in WADA's Compliance Monitoring Program.

Cricket's return to the Olympic Games has moved its governing body into anti-doping's strictest category. The World Anti-Doping Agency has upgraded the International Cricket Council (ICC) to tier 1 under its prioritisation policy owing to cricket's Olympic inclusion, while India remained in the top tier of signatories that face the strictest scrutiny in the body's Compliance Monitoring Program, according to The Bridge.

The ICC was in tier 2 until now. The new tiers, covering International Federations, National Anti-Doping Organisations and Major Event Organisations, come into effect from January 1 next year.

Why the tier changed

"IF tiers are based on whether sports are included in the Olympic or Paralympic programs and on their combined Minimum Levels of Analysis (MLAs) taken from the Technical Document for Sport Specific Analysis (TDSSA)."

https://www.instagram.com/p/De-hTLYo1IX/ — World Anti-Doping Agency

The MLA covers a percentage of the total number of eligible tests done on international-level athletes and applies to testing conducted by all anti-doping organisations. Cricket will return to the Olympic roster at the 2028 Los Angeles Games, its first appearance since Paris 1900 — a status change that, under WADA's rules, automatically raises the compliance bar for the sport's federation.

The ICC has been a WADA signatory since July 2006, and its anti-doping code — compliant with the WADA Code — is built to maintain the integrity of cricket, protect participants' health and rights and keep the sport free from doping, according to the ICC.

What tier 1 requires

The strict compliance code includes timely sample collection, proper pursuit of all whereabouts failures and potential anti-doping rule violations, and adherence to provisions for a fair hearing within a reasonable time by an impartial, operationally independent panel. Federations in the top tier face a stricter mechanism under which procedures can be initiated against them if they do not correct critical requirements related to testing, results management and Therapeutic Use Exemption entries within the three-month deadline specified in the International Standard for Code Compliance by Signatories.

In practical terms, national boards — including the BCCI — will feel this through testing volume and paperwork discipline long before LA 2028: more out-of-competition testing, tighter whereabouts compliance for top players, and less tolerance for late TUE filings. With Olympic medals now attached to T20 cricket, anti-doping is no longer a side office in the sport. It is part of qualification.
